item.title: Alpitronic builds DC fast charger factory in South Carolina, USA
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Alpitronic is expanding its presence in the USA and investing nearly US$34 million in its own production facility for fast-charging stations in South Carolina. Additionally, the South Tyrolean charging infrastructure specialist is strengthening its North America management with Christopher Balcom as the new Chief Commercial Officer.

item.title: ‘Nova’: Moment Energy launches second-life battery storage system
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Canadian battery technology firm Moment Energy has unveiled Nova, a new battery energy storage system (BESS) built using repurposed EV batteries. The system is now in production at the company's Megafactory 1, with orders open and initial deliveries planned for Q1 2027.

item.title: Tesla opens its first public Megacharger in Texas
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The new Megacharger is the first opened by Tesla in Texas, and adds eight high-powered charging stalls capable of delivering up to 1.2 MW each. The site is located in Mesquite, east of Dallas, and extends the company's public truck charging network into one of the largest freight markets in the US.

item.title: TotalEnergies to install 1,500 EV charging points in London
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: TotalEnergies has been selected to install over 1,500 new public EV charging points in the London Borough of Tower Hamlets over the next four years. This project marks the first charging contract in London to receive funding from the Government's LEVI scheme.

item.title: Compact premium: first drive in the new Audi A2 e-tron
item.dc:creator: Robin Engelhardt
item.description: With the A2 e-tron, Audi is introducing a compact car to the market that doesn’t neatly fit into any of the classic categories. In Audi’s internal logic, it is set to replace both the A1 and the Q2. For Volkswagen, it is another MEB derivative. For the general public, it is primarily the successor to the cult classic original A2 from 1999. We took a close look at the compact premium speedster for a day, testing both the 125 kW entry-level model and the 240 kW top version.

item.title: Tesla plant manager André Thierig faces penalty order following dispute with IG Metall
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The Fürstenwalde/Spree district court has issued a penalty order against André Thierig, head of Tesla Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg, for defamation. Thierig had claimed in February that a works council meeting had been illegally recorded, a claim the IG Metall union denies. Thierig has already filed an objection against the penalty order.

item.title: Envision AESC surpasses production volume milestone for 46120 battery cells
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Envision AESC states that it has now delivered over 10 million units of its cylindrical 46120 battery cells. Series production at the Chinese plants in Jiangsu and Hebei began in July 2026. The BMW iX5 has been confirmed as the first model to use these cells.

item.title: Sila secures billion-dollar offtake agreement with Panasonic
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: US battery material manufacturer Sila will supply Panasonic Energy with its silicon-carbon anode material, Titan Silicon, in the future. The multi-year agreement could reach a volume of over one billion US dollars.

item.title: POSCO expands lithium business with major order from CATL
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The South Korean industrial conglomerate POSCO is supplying Chinese battery leader CATL with lithium for electric vehicles through a new three-year contract until 2028. With the agreement now underway, POSCO continues to strengthen its market position in China.

item.title: 2027 Bentley Torcal eSUVs sell out
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: With the Torcal, Bentley has ventured into the world of pure electric vehicles for the first time. Even before production of the luxury SUV begins, it appears the automaker has succeeded, as the units planned for 2027 production are already sold out.

item.title: BMW iX5 enters series production
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: BMW has launched series production of its mid-size electric SUV, the BMW iX5. According to US media reports, around 70 vehicles per day are currently rolling off the production line at the Spartanburg plant in South Carolina. For 2027, an annual production of 60,000 units is expected.

item.title: Ford delivers first LFP batteries for test fitting in Fathom prototypes
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Ford has begun production of LFP cells at the BlueOval Battery Park in Michigan. They are being transported to the vehicle plant in Louisville, where they will initially be used in prototypes of the Ford Fathom. The E-pickup, the first representative of the new Universal EV Platform, is scheduled to enter series production in 2027.

item.title: Sany eTrucks: Targeting Europe with 500 km ranges – and competitive pricing
item.dc:creator: Peter Schwierz
item.description: SANY aims to establish itself in Europe with electric trucks - and is doing so with considerable confidence. At the IAA Transportation in Hanover, the Chinese manufacturer outlined its ambitions for the European market. In a video interview, Kevin Eichele, Head of Product and Business Development for SANY eTrucks in Europe, discusses range, delivery times, service, and an extremely aggressive pricing strategy.

item.title: Bosch to manufacture electric drivetrains for trucks in Brazil
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Bosch will start producing electric motors for trucks and trailers at its Campinas plant from 2027. Additionally, the company has signed an agreement with Suspensys, a Randoncorp Group company, to collaborate on electrified drive axles in Latin America.

item.title: RATP Dev to grow share of e-buses in Nancy public transport fleet
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: From January 2027, RATP Dev will operate public transport in and around the French city of Nancy for seven years. The operator aims to increase the share of battery buses and trolleybuses in the 257-vehicle fleet from 11 to 35 per cent by 2033.

item.title: Cylib opens door for investment by German Federal Agency for Disruptive Innovation
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: SPRIND, the German Federal Agency for Disruptive Innovation, is participating in Aachen-based battery recycling specialist Cylib. The startup, founded in 2022, is close to commercialising its processes. Cylib's hydrometallurgical recycling plant is currently being built in Dormagen, North Rhine-Westphalia.

item.title: VinFast unveils new VF 5 and VF 6 with refreshed design, improved range
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Vietnamese automaker VinFast has unveiled facelifted versions of the VF 5 and VF 6 small electric SUVs, both with revised styling, longer driving ranges, and new quality-of-life features. The company has launched both updated EVs first in its home market and expects to commence deliveries after Lunar New Year, which falls on 6 February 2027.

item.title: Volgren delivers 95 electric buses to Transport for NSW
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Australian bus manufacturer Volgren has completed delivery of 95 battery-electric buses to Transport for NSW. The fleet was delivered in just seven months and will be operated by Transit Systems Australia from the Leichhardt depot in Sydney.

item.title: GM adds ‘plug & charge’ to Electrify America charging hubs
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: EV drivers enrolled in GM's Energy Pass service now have access to 'plug & charge' capabilities at participating Electrify America fast-charging hubs in the US. This allows compatible vehicles to start charging simply by connecting the cable - without the need for an app, touchscreen or payment card.

item.title: New Jersey awards nearly $15 million for electric schoolbuses
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) has awarded nearly $15 million in grants to school districts and transport providers to purchase 44 battery-electric schoolbuses and install 40 associated charging stations.

item.title: EU statistics reveal sales trends for battery-electric trucks and tractor units
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The sales of electric commercial vehicles vary depending on the vehicle structure: conventional trucks already account for a higher share of electric vehicles than tractors. This is revealed by an analysis of the Federal Statistical Office, drawing on data from the European statistical authority Eurostat.

item.title: BAIC sells 112 battery swap stations, shifts focus to CATL
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: BAIC plans to sell assets related to 112 of its own battery swap stations as it more closely aligns its swap strategy with CATL's Choco-Swap network. The minimum price for the package is approximately 278 million yuan.

item.title: Uber and Momenta test autonomous taxi in Munich
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Mobility provider Uber and AI technology company Momenta have launched a joint project for autonomous passenger transport in Munich. During the test phase, the service is limited to a designated area in northern Munich. For safety reasons, specialised personnel must accompany the autonomous vehicle for monitoring.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz VLE production finalises in China
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Three months after applying for local sales approval, the first series-production vehicles of the new electric VLE van are now rolling off the production line at Mercedes-Benz's Chinese plant. With this, the Stuttgart-based automaker is setting the stage for the market launch in the People's Republic just before the public premiere at the Guangzhou Auto Show.

item.title: E.ON and BMW expand V2G offering for Neue Klasse models
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: In addition to the pioneering BMW iX3, further models from the Neue Klasse series can now use V2G functions. The technical prerequisite is the sixth generation BMW eDrive technology, which debuted with the iX3.

item.title: BMZ integrates digital battery passports into series production
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: BMZ, together with Minespider, is introducing digital battery passports for its EU production in Germany and Poland. The passports are to be created directly using production data and will meet the requirements of the EU Battery Regulation starting February 2027.

item.title: VW secures trademark rights for ‘ID. UP’
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: A new entry from VW has appeared at the EUIPO, the EU Intellectual Property Office. The company has applied to register the name ID. UP. This suggests that the upcoming electric model will also bear this name. A report from Portugal already mentions the production of the first pre-series vehicles.

item.title: EU accelerates approvals for power grids and charging stations
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The European Parliament and EU member states have reached a provisional agreement to streamline approval procedures for grid connections, charging stations, storage systems, and more. As part of this, the construction of charging stations with up to one megawatt in "artificial structures" is expected to become exempt from approval in the future.

item.title: Envoy and LACI launch EV car-sharing initiative in New Jersey
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The partners will deploy up to 30 shared EVs in Hudson and Bergen counties. An $8.5 million (around €7.8 million) state grant funds the project to expand electric mobility in underserved communities.

item.title: Rolls-Royce Phantom VI swaps V8 for electric powertrain
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Electrogenic has converted a 1973 Rolls-Royce Phantom VI to electric drive. The official representative limousine of the City of London now has 120 kW of power, a 62 kWh battery and charging capacity of up to 100 kW.
